Subject: Private VPC - Recap and next steps

Hi Tara / Daniel,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. Quick recap from our discovery and proposed next steps so we can align the Private VPC workstream: 

Summary of what we heard:
- You want a fully private deployment (Customer VPC + PrivateLink or VPC Peering) to keep inference traffic off the public internet.
- Primary concerns: egress IP allowlisting for downstream partners, audit/logging retention, and separation of PHI workloads.
- Target throughput: ~15 rps sustained, occasional spikes to 40 rps.
- Timeline: Proof-of-concept in Q1 and production in Q2 if procurement/architecture approvals go well.

Questions we raised / items for your infra team to confirm:
1) Preference between PrivateLink vs VPC Peering (we can support either; PrivateLink simplifies routing but may have some cross-account setup overhead).
2) Whether you need fixed outbound egress IPs for the service (we can provide static egress ranges from our NAT layer when using PrivateLink or reserved egress for Dedicated deployments).
3) Your allowed CIDR ranges / existing firewall rules for inbound to the PrivateLink endpoint (if applicable).

Attachments: redwood-private-vpc-checklist.pdf (simple checklist we use for network calls).

Proposed next steps:
- Schedule a 45-min technical network call with your cloud ops / netops (Daniel) and our infra engineer (Sean).
- I'll share a short network checklist to help Daniel collect diagrams / ACL entries ahead of the call.
- If procurement wants an initial SOW/quote for Dedicated capacity (as an option), I can get that started — please let me know a contact.

Would next Thursday (12/30) or the week of 01/03 work for a deep-dive?

Thanks,

Marissa Cole

Hi Marissa,

Appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side after syncing with Daniel: 

- LumenHealth prefers PrivateLink for isolation reasons — our security team has standardized on interface endpoints for third-party services where possible.
- We do need stable outbound (egress) IPs for several partners (analytics and reporting) so that they can whitelist traffic. Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide a small set of static egress IPs when the deployment is configured via PrivateLink?
- Attached: lumen_vpc_diagram.png (high-level VPC/subnet layout). Daniel will join the technical call.

Procurement has copied in an initial SOW contact (procurement@lumenhealth.com) — they will want an outline of costs for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (on-prem) options.

For scheduling, 01/05 or 01/06 in the morning PST works best for Daniel.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Private VPC - Networking & PrivateLink questions

Tara / Daniel — thanks for the note and the diagram, that helps a lot. Quick answers and proposed next steps before our technical call on 01/06: 

1) Egress IPs: Yes — when configured with PrivateLink we can publish a small set of static egress IP ranges from our NAT/egress layer. For Dedicated customers we can also reserve fixed egress IPs. I'll include the exact CIDR(s) on the call; typical allocations are /29 or /28 depending on needs.

2) Ingress allowlist: For PrivateLink you need to allow our interface endpoint address (we'll provide the private IP and service name). For VPC peering we'd provide the peered prefixes. Sample allowlist entry (example):
- Protocol: TCP
- Destination: 10.32.15.0/28 (Redwood PrivateLink endpoint - sample)
- Ports: 443 (TLS)

3) Monitoring/audit logs: We can forward request logs to your S3/Syslog or provide a syslog endpoint; Redwood retains request traces for the retention window in the contract, and we can extend retention for regulatory needs.

Next steps I propose for the 01/06 call (I'll send a calendar invite):
- Brief 15-min intro (Marissa + Tara + Daniel + Sean)
- 30-min deep technical review (Sean to cover endpoint setup, IP ranges, egress options; Vivek to cover Dedicated sizing/throughput guidance)
- Action items: deliver explicit egress CIDRs, example CloudFormation for PrivateLink integration, and a first-cut Dedicated cost estimate for procurement.

HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/5482/D-2027-0842

Attachment: redwood-private-vpc-checklist.pdf (again)

See you on 01/06 at 09:00 PST (invite sent).

Best,
